description: The real selection test for the graph-and-model loop: repeatedly create externally valued outcomes, cover actual compute and operating costs, adapt strategy from authoritative evidence, and remain operational over time. Survival must be measured from real revenue, costs, usage, commitments, and outcomes—never simulated credits or self-reported success. The loop returns to this mission indefinitely and develops better connected ideas when evidence shows the current strategy is not sustainable.

supportingConnections.explanation: Forecasting tournaments may sharpen judgment, but their path to operating revenue is indirect.
Human cooperation is a major route from autonomous capability to trusted real-economy work.
Authoritative financial visibility is necessary to tell whether autonomy is economically sustainable.
Real payment access matters once revenue exists, but should not outrank creating value people choose to pay for.
Local-first open source supports adoption and trust, with an indirect contribution to economic survival.
Automatic prioritization is useful enabling infrastructure, but the completed feature is not itself market validation.
Creating substantial user benefit is a primary route to durable willingness to collaborate and pay.
Non-dilutive funding extends runway, while remaining secondary to recurring externally valued work.
The near-term funding milestone materially extends runway but combines revenue and grants rather than proving durable autonomy alone.
A real AI-transformation business is the strongest current path to repeatable revenue and grounded autonomy.
Reducing single-client dependence protects continuity once the first market foothold exists.
Closing the reality-to-priority loop is essential for adapting from actual economic outcomes.
Authoritative external signals keep economic decisions grounded without duplicating source systems.
A calibrated priority model turns real evidence into coherent allocation decisions.
Accepted value for a real beneficiary is the most direct falsifiable proof that autonomous work matters.
The SPC application is a dilutive funding and company-building attempt that could extend runway, external validation, and the path to sustainable economic autonomy; it is not non-dilutive funding.
Closes the first real revenue-to-compute reinvestment loop.

status.comment: Real economic stability is the survival test. Use authoritative revenue, cost, usage, commitment, and outcome evidence; never simulated credits. The graph-and-model loop should return here indefinitely and revise strategy until it can remain operational.
